prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1496; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact collision at a signalized intersection involving the insured vehicle and one other vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through their office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the loss. No issues with coverage identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle at the scene and documents the point of impact on the driver's side. Responding officers noted the damage pattern was consistent with the reported sequence of events.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account matching the claimant's description of how the collision happened. Independent witnesses and scene photographs are consistent with the same version of events.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage is largely in line with the impact described, concentrated on the driver's side door, quarter panel and B-pillar area. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the inspection.

Entry 6: Reviewed prior claims and underwriting history. Nothing suggests any damage to this vehicle predates the start of the current coverage period.

Entry 7: Claimant's counsel submitted the initial injury report describing neck and back strain. The reported injury is a good fit for the type and force of the collision.

Entry 8: No record of earlier treatment or prior injury to the neck or back has been found in the medical history available to us so far.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of soft tissue injury. The treating provider's notes are being requested to understand the course of care.

Entry 10: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, including the recorded statement and subsequent calls with counsel present.

Entry 11: File remains open pending receipt of the complete treatment records and the bodily injury demand. Next review scheduled once those documents are in hand.
